sections.html:
Greenwood lies in Johnson County, roughly 11 miles south of downtown Indianapolis and wedged between Interstate 65 and Interstate 69. Franklin, the county seat, is 12 miles further south. At the 2020 census the city had 63,830 people, a 28.2 percent rise over 2010. All that growth means plenty of Greenwood houses are newer than the stock in Indiana's older cities, though the age mix changes by neighborhood.

The city's job base leans on retail, services and distribution: Greenwood Park Mall, an Amazon fulfillment center near Worthsville Road and I-65, and the U.S. headquarters of Endress+Hauser. When someone's job changes or their employer transfers them, a firm sale date can suddenly matter more than the top price.

Greenwood has hot summers and cold winters. July highs average 85.2 degrees, January lows 22.9, and a normal year drops about 45 inches of precipitation. That swing punishes roofs, siding, driveways and air conditioning units.

Pleasant Run Creek cuts across the north half of the city from east to west. Own a house up there? Look at the current flood map before you list.

Roof and HVAC condition count whatever the age of the house. A financed buyer may ask you to repair them. A cash buyer weighs the same items and folds the cost into the offer.

Inspections and reported violationsCode Enforcement, 300 S. Madison Ave.317-887-5000
Permits, inspections, unsafe structuresBuilding Division, 300 S. Madison Ave.317-887-5230

Greenwood's Planning staff deal with zoning, site plan review, land alteration permits and sign permits. If a zoning decision is contested, appeals go to the Advisory Plan Commission and the Board of Zoning Appeals. Fire code is enforced separately from building inspection.

If a rental is what you are selling, phone Code Enforcement at 317-887-5000 and ask whether any registration applies.

An open violation will not block a sale, yet you should learn what is open on your address ahead of time so the title company hears it from you first. Cash buyers can often take the property with the issue left as it is.

Johnson County mails Greenwood owners a property tax bill split into two installments. Under the 2026 schedule those fall on May 11 and November 10. Pay within 30 days after a due date and the penalty is 5 percent; wait longer and it climbs to 10 percent. The county treasurer collects.

A bill still unpaid when you sell is cleared out of your proceeds at closing. Because an installment may land close to your closing date, ask the title company how it will be shared with the buyer.

Indiana deed transfers go with a sales disclosure form. The assessor in the county reviews it and the auditor files it, and the recorder will not accept the deed unless proof of the auditor's receipt comes with it. Details of this routine have been revised, so your title company can give you the steps in force now.

A different chapter of state law, IC 32-21-5, deals with the seller's disclosure form and has a section on presenting it before an offer is accepted. Whether it covers your sale is a question for your agent or attorney.

Greenwood children attend schools run by one of three corporations: Greenwood Community School Corporation, Clark-Pleasant or Center Grove. The street address settles which, and buyers notice, so check it before you write up the property.

On the east side of the city, I-65 has exits 97, 99 and 101. I-69 has exits 156 and 158 just beyond the western city limits. U.S. 31 and State Road 135 run north and south. For transit, IndyGo routes 16, 29 and 31 reach northern Greenwood, and Access Johnson County runs buses.

The owners who call us tend to hold a house that needs updating, an inherited property, a rental or a deadline.

  • Aging systems: roofs, furnaces and water heaters close to the end of their life.
  • Inherited property: heirs often live elsewhere and do not want to look after a vacant house.
  • Rentals: tenants and lease terms limit when a house can be shown.
  • Timing: a new job or a move across the Indianapolis area can fix the date.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
1. Share the address and basic facts: condition, occupancy, any loan balance.
  2. We walk through the Greenwood house and present an offer.
  3. If you accept, the title company opens the file and searches the deed.
  4. You sign the sales disclosure form and the deed.
  5. The deed is recorded, taxes owed are paid, and you receive the balance.

Delays almost always come from title problems such as an old lien or a name on the deed that has not been updated. Raising these on the first call gives the title company time to fix them.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
We buy Greenwood houses as-is: no repair list, no showings. Tell us about the house, let us look at it and take our offer. Once you accept, a title company checks the deed for liens and unpaid taxes, prepares the disclosure form and picks a closing date. Money reaches you at closing, after any tax owed is paid.

Set that against a listing, with its lender-driven repairs and the months a house can sit. Before the first call, gather your tax bill, any lease and your mortgage payoff figures. Ask for the closing date in writing.

sections.h2: Selling a house that needs repairs
sections.html: You can list it and negotiate repairs with a financed buyer, or ask for a cash offer on the house as-is. List the work a buyer's inspector would flag, such as the roof, furnace, water heater, siding and driveway, and get rough estimates. Subtract those from a listing price, add the cost of waiting, and set the result beside the cash number. Pick the route that fits your timing.

A vacant house still costs money. Utilities, insurance, lawn care and property tax keep arriving, and an empty house can draw break-ins or burst pipes in a hard freeze. Heirs who live out of town often find that a quick as-is sale ends the monthly drain and the trips back. Gather the estate papers, the tax bill and any keys, then talk with the title company about what the deed needs before closing.

faqs.q: Where is Greenwood, IN, in relation to Indianapolis?
faqs.a: Greenwood is about 11 miles south of downtown Indianapolis, in Johnson County. It sits between I-65 and I-69, and the county seat, Franklin, is 12 miles to the south.
Call Code Enforcement at 317-887-5000 to ask before selling a rental. The city has a Code Enforcement office and a Building Division.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments a year, in May and November. A 5 percent penalty applies within 30 days after the date, and 10 percent after that. Pay the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a building permit in Greenwood?
faqs.a: The Building Division at 300 S. Madison Ave., phone 317-887-5230. It handles building permits, inspections and unsafe structure investigations.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwood house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it and negotiate repairs with a financed buyer, or you can ask for a cash offer on the house as-is. Compare the net amounts and the timing.
